Resolved by deletion, 2026-08-26.

The sidecar was a hand-written file duplicating a fact the wheel already
carries, and nothing consumed it. I searched the whole tree: no code, no
Makefile target, no runbook and no test reads dist/*.whl.sha256. The only
mentions are release records observing whether it happened to agree - and the
security review says so itself: 'the generator that can produce it is still
unfixed'. There is no generator. A person typed it.

It is also now redundant. Since techtree-python-5uq the cross-repository gate
hashes the wheel it is handed and compares that to the digest the bootstrap
document publishes (check 26, bootstrap_cli_wheel_sha256). The published
coordinate is therefore checked against the actual bytes, which is the thing
the sidecar was standing in for.

So the file is deleted rather than regenerated: a hand-maintained copy of a
digest can only ever be a chance to be wrong about it, and preferring
deletion over policing is the standing rule. dist/ is git-ignored, so this
needs no commit. Recorded on techtree-python-as0 that no sidecar is to be
recreated at the freeze.

There was nothing to change: no runbook, contract or document in the tree
publishes an install command with --force. The finding is a hazard of release
engineering practice, not a defect in shipped code, so the fix is a binding
rule rather than a patch.

It is now written into docs/decisions/0031, which is binding: release and
acceptance rebuild one version number repeatedly, `uv tool install --force`
can serve a stale cached wheel of that same version while exiting zero and
printing "Installed 1 package", so every runbook and acceptance step that
installs a locally built wheel uses --reinstall and checks the build
provenance the program reports against the wheel it meant to install before
any paid step.

The vom worker's brief carries the same instruction for its own isolated
install, and WP11h's runbook inherits it from the decision.
